## Appendix B Limitations

We note three limitations of MoFlow. First, it compares value vectors through the linear score {\bm{w}}^{\top}{\bm{v}} , so it covers the convex hull of the Pareto front but not its concave regions, which only nonlinear scalarizations (e.g., Chebyshev) can reach. Second, like AFlow (Zhang et al., 2025d), it requires a manually designed operator pool for each task. With a large open pool, the trial budget alone could not substitute for a stronger proposer. Third, to save cost, every online search stops early once the hypervolume of the executed front plateaus (Appendix D), a rule that halted all reported runs between trials 40 and 50, so we never observe MoFlow (online) under a substantially larger budget. Moreover, the fixed operator pool and horizon bound the structurally distinct workflows the search can reach (even though free-form roles leave the raw workflow set unbounded), so additional trials would likely revisit the front rather than extend it.

## Appendix C MoFlow Details

Appendix C.1 gives the state and action spaces of the MOMDP together with the prompt templates, and Appendix C.2 the full search procedure.

### C.1 Construction MOMDP and Prompt Templates

#### State representation.

A state is an immutable WorkflowGraph. Two partial workflows with the same structure share a canonical key and map to the same node, so a workflow reachable by different edit sequences is visited only once.

#### Action space.

An action is one of three atomic edits.

• 

AddOperator( o , width, role) appends operator o from the task’s operator pool (below). The role is a free-text label that names the node’s prompt archetype (e.g., “step-by-step solver” or “code verifier”).

• 

AddControl(branch | loop, width) wraps an operator in a control structure: branch runs width parallel attempts and keeps the best, while loop refines sequentially for width rounds.

• 

Terminate closes the workflow.

Roles are not edited independently. The proposer assigns an initial role when it proposes each node-adding edit, and the realizer rewrites that role into up to N_{r} distinct specializations when the edit is instantiated (realizer prompt below). An edit is legal only if it yields a valid workflow: a terminal workflow cannot be extended, Terminate requires a non-empty graph whose last operator emits an answer (e.g., Generate or Ensemble), widths are bounded, and depth cannot exceed the horizon H . These constraints define the legal action set A(s) .
